author: Gmelin, 1789

months.note: 5월에 와서 10월까지 머물며, 알은 5월 하순~8월 상순에 낳는다.

summary: 우리나라에서 드물게 번식하는 여름철새로, 갈대밭이나 물가 풀숲에서 홀로 또는 암수가 함께 지낸다. 물가 풀숲이나 관목림의 갈대, 줄풀 줄기 사이에 접시 모양 둥지를 틀고, 알 5~6개를 낳아 17~19일 동안 품는다. 물고기를 주로 먹고 개구리와 새우 같은 갑각류도 먹는다. 온대에서 열대에 걸쳐 번식하며 한국과 유라시아 대륙 동남부에 분포한다.

points.en: black crown from forehead to nape (male)
pale rufous-brown cheeks and ear coverts
white chin and sides of throat

young: 어른 암컷과 비슷하나 머리꼭대기가 검지 않고 머리·목·등·날개덮깃에 짙은 갈색 세로줄무늬가 많으며, 아랫면의 세로줄무늬도 더 진하다.

similar.how: 큰덤불해오라기 수컷은 등이 어두운 밤색이고 날개의 검은색과 담황색 대비가 약하지만, 덤불해오라기는 등이 옅은 황갈색이고 날 때 담황색 날개덮깃과 검은 날개깃이 뚜렷이 대비된다.

art.subject: Yellow Bittern (Ixobrychus sinensis), adult male in summer, as seen in Korean reed beds from May to August: crown black from the forehead to the nape; face, ear coverts and neck sides pale rufous-buff; chin and sides of the throat white; foreneck and underparts buffy-white with faint buff stripes; mantle and back warm brown; wing coverts pale yellowish-buff, contrasting with blackish flight feathers; tail black. Bill long and dagger-shaped, yellow with a dark upper ridge; bare lores yellow-green; iris yellow; legs and feet pale greenish-yellow.
art.pose: clinging to reed stems above the water, side view
art.scene: Korean summer reedbed along a pond edge, with tall green reeds and wild rice; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging to reeds: black crown, pale rufous-brown cheeks and ear coverts, white chin and throat sides, warm brown back, whitish-buff underparts, black tail, pale greenish-yellow legs
adult male, flight side view from above: pale buff wing coverts contrasting with blackish flight feathers, black tail, brown back
art.build: Very small heron, 37cm, a little longer than a pigeon and much slimmer. Neck long but usually drawn in; stretches it upright with the bill pointing up when alarmed. Bill straight, sharp and dagger-like, longer than the head. Legs medium length, greenish-yellow, with long toes for gripping reeds. Climbs and clings to reed stems, often straddling two stems above the water. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail very short. Flies low over the reeds; the pale buff wing coverts contrast with black flight feathers and tail.
avoid: Do not paint the whole upperparts and wings chestnut; that is Cinnamon Bittern, which lacks black flight feathers.
Do not paint a black or dark chestnut back; those mark Little Bittern and Schrenck's Bittern males.
Do not draw long plumes or an upright, long-legged egret posture.
